extension.name: Assure
extension.description: Make QA part of the Spec Kit lifecycle: initialize project policy, require feature test-readiness analysis before implementation, and generate a current QA test manual before pull-request creation.
extension.author: Samy K. Abushanab

dependents.name: Pull Request Workflow
dependents.description: Generate or update pull requests from Spec Kit artifacts, enforce installed QA and User Manual freshness policies, then process review feedback through an approval-gated fix and reply workflow.
dependents.author: Samy K. Abushanab

pageProps.readmeContent: # QA (`assure`) **Purpose:** make QA part of the Spec Kit lifecycle. Assure finds missing test and evidence work before implementation, and writes a QA walkthrough for testers after it. | | | | --- | --- | | Lifecycle phase | After `tasks`, before and after `implement` | | Hooks | Three optional hooks; Assure Init can make the analysis hook mandatory ([hooks](../reference/hooks.md)) | | Commands | `init`, `analyze`, `document` ([reference](../reference/commands.md#assure)) | | Requires | Illustrate 2.x, enforced by `deps.py ensure`; Python 3.11 or later | | Standalone | Yes | | License | MIT | ## Setup ```bash specify extension add illustrate specify extension add assure ``` ```text /speckit-assure-init Configure required QA analysis and tester documentation for the booking application. ``` Init asks for **integrated** or **manual** mode. Integrated mode, the recommended choice, makes the `before_implement` analysis mandatory and tells PR to refresh QA documentation when it is stale. In the managed Workflow, select QA through `/speckit-workflow-init` instead. ## Example ```text /speckit-assure-analyze --feature specs/412-refund-approval Add missing duplicate settlement, rejection, permission and accessibility coverage. /speckit-assure-document --feature specs/412-refund-approval Document runnable refund scenarios and the actual test evidence. ``` You get the missing tasks, tester steps, synthetic test data, expected results, and screenshots where there is evidence. Freshness records are kept under `.specify/extensions/assure/state/`. ## How it runs ![Assure sequence: assure.init sets the required or manual policy; assure.analyze checks readiness and adds missing tasks; you implement and run your project's tests; assure.document records steps and observed evidence; a freshness check flags changed code that needs an update.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samykabu/sanduq/main/docs/diagrams/extension-assure.animated.svg) Configured hooks or the managed dispatcher call Analyze and Document. In manual mode you run them yourself. Your project's checks supply the test results; Assure records them. [Editable source](../diagrams/extension-assure.html). Scripts do the mechanical parts. `assure_scan.py` detects the projects in the repository and keeps `.github/memory/project-memory.md` current: Analyze only reads the result, Document writes it. It skips the folders under `scan.exclude` in `assure-config.yml`, whose default list also covers `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, `target`, `vendor`, `Pods` and `.gradle`. Inside a git work tree it also skips the folders git ignores. `assure_scan.py --check` prints the inventory and the `would write` line without writing; add `--show-block` to also print the memory block. Init keeps an existing `assure-config.yml` and changes only its three lifecycle values. `audit_qa.py` checks the generated manual for image alt text and captions, broken relative links, the development-only marker, and secret-shaped values. When Document runs again, the freshness status lists the changed inputs and outputs, so only the affected parts are rewritten. The `documentation-gates.yml` CI check checks out the PR head, not GitHub's merge commit, and runs `assure_state.py status --gate`, which skips the check when `lifecycle.require_document_before_pr` is false. Init replaces an unedited earlier `documentation-gates.yml`; for an edited one it prints the `ref:` line to add. ## Limits - Assure writes test documentation. It does not prove that tests passed. - A walkthrough goes stale when the implementation changes. Run Document again. - QA documentation is for testers. It is not the end-user manual. - The old `qa` and `how-to-test` extension IDs are retired. Package details: [Assure README](../../extensions/assure/README.md).
